ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended most recently by the Law of 10 July 2020 (implementing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and its implementing grand-ducal regulations; Law of 13 February 2018 (transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849); CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended, and related CSSF AML/CFT circulars; Articles 710-1 et seq. of the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (SARL formation, capital and seat requirements); AML/CFT obligations of Luxembourg notaries pursuant to the Law of 9 December 1976 on the organisation of the notariat.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners is accessible to competent authorities and to persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; unrestricted public access has been suspended following the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 in joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft Articles of Association (statuts constitutifs) of the SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary appointed in Luxembourg (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Luxembourg by a duly appointed Luxembourg notary (no apostille required for the domestic deed)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each shareholder, manager, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or civil registry authority in the country of residence of the individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization where the country of origin is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or recent bank statement, issued within the last three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local utility provider or regulated bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or notarized certification acceptable to the Luxembourg notary and RBE filing agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for incorporation formalities and RBE filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin or Luxembourg notary office accepting the foreign power
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by Luxembourg notarial legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds documentation for the initial share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-stamped certification acceptable to the Luxembourg notary and AML/KYC officer (apostille not generally required for bank-issued letters, but notarization may be requested)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced customer due diligence requiring screening of all UBOs, directors, managers and authorized signatories against the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) references, the EU consolidated list of persons and entities subject to financial sanctions, the EU terrorist list, the UN Security Council 1267/1988 and 1718 sanctions lists, the OFAC SDN list and the OFAC 50% ownership rule, and domestic PEP databases; confirmed PEP status triggers senior-management approval, enhanced ongoing monitoring, and documented source-of-funds verification before incorporation proceeds; adverse database hits result in automatic escalation, refusal of the engagement, and filing of a suspicious transaction report with the CRF where required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online platform - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); public and filing portal accessible via lbr.lu and rcs.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name of a Luxembourg SARL may be chosen in French, German, or Luxembourgish, optionally combined with words in any other language, and must be written in the Latin alphabet; the legal suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' must be appended unless already fully contained in the name; the name must be distinctive within the RCS, must not mislead as to the legal form or activity, and must not be contrary to public policy or good morals; special characters and diacritical marks are permitted but must be reconcilable with the RCS transliteration standard for European business registers so that the name can be reliably reproduced in standard Latin-script encoding.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank (prior authorization of the CSSF required)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance (prior authorization of the Commissariat aux Assurances required)
Bourse / Stock exchange / Trading venue (CSSF authorization required)
Fiduciaire / Trust company (prior authorization of the Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce required)
Fonds / OPC / SICAV / SICAR (CSSF authorization required by the amended Law of 17 December 2010)
Luxembourg / Luxembourgeois in a misleading context implying state affiliation or privilege
Union européenne / European Union / EU (authorization of the European institutions required)
Société cotée / Listed company where the SARL is not admitted to a regulated market
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its counsel may submit a reasoned remediation request to the LBR name clearance department within fifteen calendar days of the rejection notice; if the rejection is maintained, an administrative appeal may be filed by application to the First Instance Chamber (Tribunal d'arrondissement) of Luxembourg under Article 43 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies, within two months of notification of the final LBR decision; the court reviews the legality and proportionality of the refusal and may order registration of the name; a successfully reserved name may be extended for additional consecutive periods of one month in accordance with LBR administrative guidelines, generally capped at a maximum aggregate reservation period of six months, upon payment of the then-prevailing fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices without a physical presence are not permissible as the sole registered office of a Luxembourg SARL; the company must maintain a real registered office (siège statutaire) within the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg at which legal documents can be validly served, as required by the seat provisions (Articles 100 to 100-2) of the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; regulated commercial domiciliation through a licensed domiciliation agent is permitted, but the entity must evidence genuine local decision-making, local management, adequate premises, and economic substance commensurate with the re-invoicing and trading activity, consistent with Luxembourg's application of the OECD BEPS substance requirements and the domestic substance rules for financing and trading undertakings.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate (estimated 10-15% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection for a trading and re-invoicing SARL under the compliance and audit programs of the Luxembourg tax administration, the CRF and the RBE supervisory framework; the probability is materially higher where the company has limited local substance, outsourced management, or concentrated cross-border intra-group flows)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank compliance preparation charge and prevailing market fee for beneficial ownership organization charts, sanctions screening reports and KYC file assembly (approximately EUR 300 to EUR 400)

stage_1.schema_compliance_note: All statutory references relate to Luxembourg law as in force on the date of this due diligence dossier; the output is intended for Stage 1 pre-incorporation due diligence only and does not constitute tax, accounting, or post-incorporation regulatory advice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; SARL-specific provisions in Articles 710-1 to 710-25 (Chapter on Société à Responsabilité Limitée), as modernized by the Law of 23 July 2016; general corporate formation provisions of Articles 1-77; obligation to register under Articles 100-1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), administered by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Filing form for entry into the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) with compulsory dual publication in the RCS and the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL minimum subscribed capital is €12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid at incorporation; cash contributions must be deposited into and blocked on a Luxembourg (or qualifying EU/EEA) bank account until RCS registration, evidenced by an Attestation de blocage issued by the credit institution; in-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's control report (réviseur d'entreprises agréé); the blocking certificate is released to the gérant only upon presentation of the RCS registration extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founders' share subscription is ratified, the subscribed capital of €12,000 being fully paid up and blocked to the Company's order as evidenced by the Attestation de blocage issued by [Bank]. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [1, Rue de l'Exemple], L-1118 Luxembourg. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name Surname] is appointed Manager (Gérant) with sole representation authority, and is instructed to file the incorporation deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers and to procure release of the blocked capital immediately upon RCS registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Drafting of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online name search portal and Luxembourg notary drafting the statutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS/LBR electronic database to confirm that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Instruct a Luxembourg notary to prepare French-language statutes (statuts) reflecting the SARL form, the €12,000 fully paid capital, the registered office address, the share capital division, and the appointment of the first manager (gérant). For a corporate founder, obtain legalized or apostilled constitutional documents and a recent excerpt of the foreign commercial register.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name availability check against RCS/LBR
French-language draft statutes (statuts) of the SARL
Identity documents (passport or national ID) of founders
Legalized/apostilled incorporation documents and register excerpt of corporate shareholder
Power of attorney for notarial signing if the founder is not physically present
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for identity or confusion with a prior registered name, submit two alternative names and re-run the search; if the notary queries any KYC element, supplement the file with beneficial ownership, source-of-wealth and group structure documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Blocked Capital Account and Issuance of Attestation de Blocage
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g. BIL, BNP Paribas Luxembourg, Société Générale Luxembourg, Spuerkeess) acting under AML/KYC obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-operational account in the name of the SARL in formation ('SARL en formation'), remit the minimum capital of €12,000 from the founders' own accounts, and instruct the bank to issue an Attestation de blocage evidencing that the amount is ring-fenced until the RCS registration certificate is produced. The certificate must be issued within a few days before the signing of the incorporation deed and will be annexed to the constitutive act.
required_dossiers: Bank account application with beneficial ownership declaration
Founder KYC and source of funds/source of wealth documentation
Draft statutes of the SARL
Proof of wire transfer of €12,000
Attestation de blocage issued by the credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence because of the medium-risk re-invoicing/AML classification, supply the commercial contracts, pro-forma invoices, and the group organizational chart; if the application is refused, refile the same package with a second Luxembourg bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Incorporation Deed and Notarial / Registration Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary for the notarial deed (acte constitutif) with registration formalities at the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); private deed option permitted under law but notarial form is standard practice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the incorporation deed before the Luxembourg notary, either in person or through an authenticated power of attorney. The deed contains the statutes, the subscription of all shares, the appointed gérant, and the annexed Attestation de blocage. The notary registers the deed with the AEDT for signature legalization; no ad valorem contribution duty applies as the Luxembourg droit d'apport is abolished. The gérant executes the statutory declaration that the subscribed capital is fully paid and at the company's free disposal upon registration.
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation deed (acte constitutif) with annexes
Attestation de blocage issued by the bank
Manager's capital payment and free-disposal declaration under Article 710-4 of the 1915 Act
Certified identity documents of the gérant(s)
Consent letter of the appointed gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or AEDT issues an observation (e.g. missing annex, defective stake-splitting or defective capital allocation), cure the defect by an additional rectifying deed (acte rectificatif) and re-submit to the same registry office; a new bank certificate is obtained if the Attestation de blocage has expired.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) and RESA Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online e-filing portal at www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the LBR e-platform and upload the incorporation deed, the bank blocking certificate, and the standardized RCS form containing the company identification data, ISIC 4690 corporate object (general re-invoicing and wholesale trade), registered office, gérant details, and date of the constitutive deed. Submit the request for the dual RCS entry and RESA legal publication. The AEDT registry division verifies legal compliance with the 1915 Act and effects registration of the legal entity, thereby conferring legal personality.
required_dossiers: Electronic RCS incorporation filing form
Incorporation deed and consolidated annexes
Articles of association in French
Attestation de blocage from the credit institution
Certified ID copies and consents of the gérant
Initial beneficial owner declaration (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE) filed simultaneously
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS/AEDT files a query or requests corrective information, respond within the legal time period through the same LBR workspace by uploading the corrective instrument; if registration is refused, file a summary motion before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) against the refusal decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Formalities: Release of Blocked Funds, VAT / National Registration and Completion of Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS extract), Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for the national identification number and VAT number, and the credit institution releasing the blocked funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the RCS extract (extrait du RCS) attesting legal personality and the date of constitution. File the initial declaration in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) if not yet completed, and apply to the AEDT for the national ID number and VAT number; a VAT registration is required where the re-invoicing hub performs taxable intra-EU and domestic purchases/sales, while a limited taxable person regime may apply in narrow cases. Present the RCS extract to the bank to release the blocked €12,000 into the operating account, and update the corporate governance file with the statutory registers (share register, minutes register).
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
RBE initial declaration acknowledgment
AEDT application for national identification number and VAT number (standard forms)
Bank instruction letter for release of blocked funds
Statutory share register and minutes register initiated by the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT delays the VAT/national number assignment, escalate in writing and obtain a procedural acknowledgment; if the AEDT demands clarifications on the re-invoicing model, submit the commercial contracts and the Luxembourg VAT group analysis; if the bank refuses capital release, provide the RCS extract and the gérant's sworn statement under Article 710-4 to compel release.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - Ministry of the Economy, Directorate-General for Industry (Direction générale de l'industrie) would only be competent if industrial, manufacturing or warehousing premises were subsequently opened
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit required - general re-invoicing and intermediary trade under ISIC 4690 does not trigger an industrial establishment license under Luxembourg law; the RCS commercial registration itself constitutes the operating authorization for a pure trading company.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no environmental impact assessment is required for office-based re-invoicing and wholesale trade; the classified-establishments regime (établissements classés) under the Luxembourg Law of 9 June 1976 and communal environmental regulations would apply only if warehousing, storage in bulk, or physical packaging activities were later added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater, VOC, or combustion emissions are generated by an office-only re-invoicing operation; when office waste is produced, it must be collected by a licensed waste carrier in accordance with the Law of 9 June 1976, as amended, and if future warehousing is added, compliance with the Luxembourg waste code and EU Industrial Emissions Directive thresholds would become mandatory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No specific fire safety certification or structural load inspection is required for a pure administrative registered office in a standard office building; upon physical occupation, the employer must comply with the Luxembourg Labour Code, Book IV provisions on workplace safety and the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) rules, and the building owner must maintain the municipal fire safety certificates (Service d'incendie et de secours) covering emergency exits, extinguishing equipment, and electrical installations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; unified digital service portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.lu) and Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) for issuance of the 13-digit business registration number (matricule).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign entity (non-established in Luxembourg) forming or converting into a Luxembourg SARL, the sequential registration path is: (1) incorporate and file articles of association with the RCS via a Luxembourg notary, obtain the RCS registration number and 13-digit national business identifier (matricule) through MyGuichet.lu; (2) file the VAT registration application with the AEDT using official form 'Formulaire 640' (Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA), which for EU-established applicants can be done directly, whereas non-EU applicants must appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative (unless an exemption applies under Art. 65 VAT Law); (3) simultaneous registration for corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICB), and net wealth tax (IFI) is performed automatically through the RCS transmission to the ACD; (4) obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits) and, if needed, an EORI number for customs operations. Statutory deadlines: RCS filing within 1 month of formation; VAT registration must be requested before the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Luxembourg SARL is a resident capital company (société de capitaux) subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, IRC) at a headline rate of 15% plus solidarity surcharge (7% of IRC, giving 16.05% effective IRC), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, ICC) at an aggregate rate dependent on commune (typically 6.75%–11.25% for the City of Luxembourg), and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune, IFI) at 0.5% on taxable net assets with minimum IFI charges (€535 standard, but €3,210 where qualifying financial fixed assets exceed €500,000). The SARL is subject to taxation on worldwide income as a resident entity; no pass-through is available to shareholders. The territorial scope is moderated by the participation exemption regime (exemption of qualifying dividends and capital gains under Art. 166 LIR and Art. 148bis LIR) and by tax treaties. Shareholders resident abroad are subject to withholding tax on distributions (15% standard, subject to treaty relief and the Luxembourg parent-subsidiary exemption of 0% where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions or the Luxembourg participation exemption are met).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg is a civil-law jurisdiction and does not apply the US 'check-the-box' system. Recognised statutory elections include: (a) fiscal unity / group taxation ('intégration fiscale') under Art. 164bis LIR for resident groups holding at least 95% of a qualifying Luxembourg/EU/EEA subsidiary, applicable to both IRC and ICC; (b) VAT group election ('assujetti unique') under Art. 60 of the VAT Law, allowing financially, economically and organisationally linked taxable persons to file VAT as a single taxable person; (c) option to tax real estate rentals (Art. 42(3) VAT Law) for supplies to taxable persons; (d) election to apply national preferential regimes such as the IP box (Art. 50bis LIR) for qualifying intellectual property income; (e) no elective hybrid mismatch arrangements are permitted — Luxembourg implements ATAD anti-hybrid rules (Art. 168ter LIR) which operate automatically, and taxpayers may apply for an advance tax agreement (tax ruling) through the ACD's Ruling Unit (Circulaire LIR 331) to confirm tax treatment in advance. For indirect tax, an EU-established non-resident trader may register directly without a fiscal representative, while a non-EU trader requires a fiscal representative unless the transaction is a B2B reverse-charge supply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_full_list_: The legal mechanisms described above are the only available elections; there is no check-the-box election as understood under U.S. Treasury Reg. §301.7701-3. Foreign entity classification is governed solely by Luxembourg law, and hybrid mismatch outcomes are statutorily neutralised.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée / TVA), fully harmonised with Council Directive 2006/112/EC and implemented by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 (Loi modifiée du 12 février 1979 concernant la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis turnover threshold for non-established foreign suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg: VAT registration (or reverse-charge designation of a local recipient) is required from the first taxable transaction. For Luxembourg-established small enterprises, a €35,000 annual turnover exemption applies under Art. 57 VAT Law (except for certain sectors, e.g., new means of transport and specific goods). For intra-EU distance sales of goods into Luxembourg by EU sellers, the VAT registration/OSS obligation is triggered once intra-Community distance sales exceed €10,000 per calendar year (default EU threshold applicable from Luxembourg as the Member State of establishment). Cross-border B2B services supplied by a non-established trader to a Luxembourg VAT-registered customer are reverse-charged to the Luxembourg customer, and the non-established supplier has no VAT registration obligation for such supplies, though it must register if it sells goods to non-taxable persons or supplies B2C electronic services above the OSS threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance (CTC) or national mandatory e-invoicing regime is in force as of the current date. The Luxembourg Government’s transposition of the VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package is proceeding via the laws of 18 June 2024 and 12 July 2024, which introduce: (i) mandatory structured e-invoicing (Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 or Factur-X) for domestic B2B transactions between Luxembourg-established VAT payers effective from 1 January 2026; (ii) subsequent transactional data reporting (e-reporting of sales data to the AEDT) expected from 1 January 2028; and (iii) voluntary use of the EU OSS and IOSS regimes for distance sales. Currently, AEDT accepts PDF, EDI, and other unstructured formats for invoicing, while the mandatory e-invoicing obligation applies to invoices exchanged between Luxembourg-established taxable persons; cross-border e-invoicing remains governed by Directive 2014/55/EU and the receiving customer’s national rules. There is no digital stamping, QR-code clearance, or AEDT pre-approval API for invoices at this stage; implementation of the Luxembourg national e-invoicing infrastructure will require API-based clearance through the official national Peppol access point from 2026.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Art. 36 of the Luxembourg VAT Law to (a) supplies of goods dispatched or transported by or on behalf of the supplier to a destination outside the European Union (export), and (b) direct services linked to those export goods (loading, transport, brokerage, and other intermediary services). To claim 0% VAT, the evidence must establish: (i) physical export of the goods from the EU within the legally recognised period (generally the goods must leave the EU within 90 days of the supply, a practice confirmed by AEDT guidance); (ii) possession of the customs export declaration (DAU/AES) accepted by the customs office of exit; (iii) documentary proof of transport (CMR, B/L, AWB, freight invoice) and of the supplier’s ownership / legal power to dispose of the goods; (iv) for intra-EU supplies, a valid customer VAT identification number confirmed via VIES and inclusion in the recapitulative statement/EC Sales List; and (v) commercial documentation showing the customer’s identity, place of residence / establishment, and the nature/quantity of goods. Critical nuance for a re-invoicing hub: if the Luxembourg SARL acts purely as an intermediary that never touches the goods (e.g., goods move from a third-country supplier directly to a third-country buyer), the transaction creates no Luxembourg VAT nexus, and the margin is taxable as a service in Luxembourg only if the recipient or the place of effective use qualifies under Luxembourg B2B place-of-supply rules; physical export zero-rating is available only where the goods are actually exported from the EU by the Luxembourg taxable person. The zero-rating of services under Art. 36(3) VAT Law is available for transport, handling, and commission services directly connected to export goods, provided the services are rendered directly to the exporter/consignee and the goods are in the course of export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Document Administratif Unique / DAU, issued through the AES/ECS export system, evidencing the export exit and the exporter's EORI number)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Airway Bill (AWB) or CMR (Convention Marchandises Routières) transport document evidencing physical movement out of the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate and/or bank SWIFT MT103 evidencing settlement of the export sales proceeds
Commercial invoice, purchase order, sales contract, and packing list (consistency of weights, values, and descriptions with the customs declaration)
Proof of customer status: valid EU VAT identification number (VIES validation) or third-country customer certificate/registration
Recapitulative statement (EC Sales List) and Intrastat declaration for intra-EU supplies, where applicable
Freight and insurance invoices, warehouse receipts, or terminal handling receipts evidencing the transport chain
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax authorities (AEDT and ACD) treat export zero-rating as a high-risk area for re-invoicing and trading intermediaries. The standard VAT assessment limitation period is 5 years from the end of the year in which the VAT became claimable; this extends to 10 years in cases of fraud, wilful misconduct, or where a VAT declaration was not filed. Where export evidence is missing or internally inconsistent, the AEDT will reclassify the supply as taxable and immediately assess VAT at the standard 17% rate plus default interest (intérêts de retard) of 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum). Administrative fines under Art. 78 of the VAT Law range up to €25,000 per offence for incorrect invoicing or failure to substantiate, and under Art. 396 of the General Tax Law (AO) tax evasion fines may reach €250,000, increased to 5 times the evaded tax for repeated or organised fraud; criminal liability extends to imprisonment of up to 5 years for serious fraud. Additionally, the AEDT may claw back intermediary-commission input VAT where the underlying transaction is not substantiated, and may impose a penalty of 10% of the VAT under-assessed for simple negligence. The Luxembourg law does not prescribe a statutory maximum deadline for FX repatriation; the 180-day parameter used in this dossier reflects a prudent contractual benchmark generally accepted by tax and AML authorities for proving the commercial substance of cross-border re-invoicing flows. Non-repatriation beyond the contractual term, without an arm’s-length explanation, will be treated as a distribution or a non-recognised transfer pricing adjustment, triggering Luxembourg withholding tax, net wealth tax, and potential administrative penalty exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Luxembourg Financial Sector Supervisory Commission (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier, CSSF) and the Ministry of Finance; as an EU member state, Luxembourg applies the euro-area foreign exchange framework administered by the European Central Bank (ECB).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full convertibility for both capital and current account transactions under the euro-area legal framework. No general exchange control restrictions exist; profit remittance, dividend distribution, capital repayment, and liquidation proceeds may be freely transferred in EUR or any convertible currency. However, the SARL must comply with anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CTF) verification requirements, Luxembourg direct tax reporting rules, and economic substance expectations for re-invoicing/treasury activities. In practice, cross-border payments require correct ECB Balance of Payments (BoP) and International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) coding, and bank transfers must be accompanied by accurate purpose codes (statistical reasons) to avoid delay or rejection. The BCL may request underlying documentation for statistical integrity, but there is no legal ceiling, prior approval, or repatriation restriction on profits or capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg does not impose any statutory export proceeds surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. All export proceeds and trade receivables, including re-invoicing income, may be retained in any currency freely, held in offshore accounts, or converted at the market exchange rate. No deadline applies for repatriation into Luxembourg. Nevertheless, the SARL engaged in re-invoicing intermediation must record all export/import settlements for VAT, CIT (corporate income tax), and statistical reporting; proceeds routed through Luxembourg should be matched against the underlying commercial contracts to satisfy substance and beneficial ownership analysis.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account for trade receipts and disbursements
Operational account with trade finance and cash management suite
Operational and trade finance account (LC issuance, confirmations, and escrow)
Operational and capital escrow account for cross-border treasury
Operational and foreign currency multi-currency account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium to Medium-High, but with legal constraints. Luxembourg has a regulated e-money institution (EMI) regime under the CSSF, allowing pass-through payment accounts and cross-border clearing without full-scale banking license. Use of non-EU fintech or unregulated EMI/PSP is not acceptable for substantive treasury operations and may trigger AML rating escalation, loss of tax substance, or bank due-diligence rejection. EU-licensed EMIs (e.g., Luxembourg-based e-money institutions or licensed payment institutions passporting from another EU state) are viable for niche collections, corporate expense cards, and high-frequency small-value payments, but the primary operating account and trade finance letters of credit (LCs) must remain with a Tier 1 credit institution. The SARL should avoid holding significant recurring trade balances in an EMI because EMIs cannot provide documentary credit services, working capital loans, NDF (non-deliverable forward) execution, or full treasury counterparty risk management.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated Luxembourg SARL, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories must generally attend an in-person onboarding interview with the compliance officer when opening a corporate account at a Luxembourg Tier 1 bank. Remote opening is possible only after initial physical verification, for renewals, or where the bank accepts a video-based KYC/AML procedure coupled with apostilled corporate documents and a depositary or notarial ID verification. For the re-invoicing entity, a face-to-face meeting is strongly recommended because the business model is classified as Medium-Risk Enhanced; banks will require commercial rationale, supply chain documentation, and proof of operational substance in Luxembourg. A Luxembourg-based registered agent may facilitate the interview, but the bank will typically require at least one director with real decision-making authority to appear physically. Foreign directors may use a Luxembourg bank's correspondent arrangement or a local notary for remote identification, but pure video-only onboarding without any physical touchpoint is uncommon and may be refused.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership chain through non-EEA intermediate holding companies or trusts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organizational chart (all countries); certified copies of certificates of incorporation, articles of association, register of shareholders, register of directors; LEI (Legal Entity Identifier) for all entities in the chain; notarized evidence of source-of-funds and source-of-wealth for each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) above 25%; tax identification numbers (TINs) and proof of tax residency for all UBOs; up-to-date UBO register extract from Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Re-invoicing business viewed as lacking economic substance, or used for invoice mills, transfer pricing manipulation, or trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan explaining the commercial rationale; actual office lease agreement in Luxembourg; payroll and social security records for Luxembourg-resident staff; minutes of board meetings held in Luxembourg; group intercompany agreements; supplier and customer commercial contracts; complete description of the physical flow of goods, billing flow, payment terms, and incoterms; transfer pricing documentation in accordance with OECD Chapter V (Master File and Luxembourg Local File); evidence of procurement, negotiation, logistics, quality control, and risk management decisions performed in Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Abnormal payment geography, mismatch between invoicing currency and settlement currency, or rapid pass-through of large amounts with little added value
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade invoices, purchase orders, bills of lading/airway bills, customs declarations (EU Single Administrative Document), warehouse receipts; full audit trail from original supplier invoice to downstream customer invoice; bank statements for both legs; justification of use of FX products or multi-currency accounts; documented margin policy (e.g., fixed mark-up or service fee); cash flow forecasts showing adequate working capital and no reliance on unexplained third-party payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure (supplier or customer located in sanctioned, tax-blacklisted, or higher-risk jurisdictions) or involvement of politically exposed persons (PEPs)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening output against EU, UN, US OFAC, and UK lists; negative news and adverse media search results; country-specific risk assessment; third-party due diligence reports (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones) on each material counterparty; corporate registers and trade references for counterparties; certificates of good standing; declaration confirming no direct or indirect connection to designated persons; PEP status confirmation and enhanced monitoring plan if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual payment instructions, such as disbursement to third-party beneficiaries not party to the underlying trade, or use of cash-heavy intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed written instruction from client; underlying trade agreement explicitly permitting direction of payment; invoice backing each payment; full correspondence with client; letters of authorization from the ultimate beneficiary; for invoice financing or receivables purchase, signed factoring/forfaiting agreement with clear assignment; KYC file on any third-party payee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the Luxembourg SARL must be executed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wires with the exact corporate name, IBAN, BIC/SWIFT, and a proper purpose code corresponding to the nature of capital (e.g., ECB BoP category 'E' for equity, or subordinated loan 'A.2' with a loan agreement). Equity share capital up to or exceeding the minimum statutory amount may be contributed in cash, in kind, or via setoff, but for bank routing the strictest anti-money-laundering practice requires the transfer to reference 'EUROPEAN UNION - CAPITAL INJECTION - SUBSCRIPTION' plus invoice or share register reference. If the contribution is by way of shareholder loan, the SARL must provide a loan agreement, board resolution, and audited audited financial projection; the transfer purpose code must reflect 'intercompany loan' to prevent misclassification as operating revenue. For quarantine of funds, banks may redirect the incoming wire to a dedicated 'capital contribution temporary account' until the UBO and source of funds (SOF) are verified; the SARL should pre-submit the corporate wallet documentation, articles, UBO register, board resolution, and source-of-funds evidence to shorten crediting. The BCL and CSSF do not require a formal FIL (foreign investment license), but sectors are not relevant; for trade intermediary no pre-approval is required beyond standard KYC and the euro-denominated clearing network (TARGET2).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border disbursements for trade settlements use the SWIFT Global Payments Innovation (gpi) infrastructure leveraging MT103 for direct bank wire transfers, commercial letters of credit (LC) via MT700 and MT720, and documentary collection (D/P, D/A) via MT400/MT750 series. The SARL treasury desk should maintain each local currency-water or EUR account and open LC terms aligned with Incoterms 2020, with purpose codes indicating import of goods, services, or commission fees. Standard clearing rails: (i) TT (telegraphic transfer) or MT103 for supplier invoice settlements, with all fields structured to enable the EUR correspondent bank to auto-match the invoice; (ii) 'DPU' (Documentary Payment Undertaking) LC under ICC UCP 600 rules for high-value or cash-cycled transactions where a confirming bank is sought; (iii) for intra-EU payments, instant SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) or standard SEPA CT instruments, which are not SWIFT but are routed via the EBA CLEARING EURO1/STEP2; (iv) for emerging-market settlements, NDF-in-HKD/CNY/INR/BRL must be accompanied by a EUR MT202 cover and a separate MT103 with the underlying shipping documents sent through the banking channel. Treasury must enforce straight-through-processing by embedding bank code, invoice reference, and trading entity code; otherwise, correspondent banks may re-route to manual compliance review, creating delay and opt-out treatment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/foreign currency FX forward contract (deliverable) with a Luxembourg or EU bank, used to lock the exchange rate on known trade receivables/payables up to the contractual maturity

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on restricted or non-fully-convertible currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL, NGN), executed against USD or EUR as reference currency, with net settlement in EUR or USD in a Luxembourg clearing zone

Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) or currency swap for matching long-term shareholder loans or intercompany financing; permissible only when underlying exposure is genuine and within the treasury policy
Plain vanilla FX swaps (swap of principal and interest currencies for a temporary period) for managing short-term cash gaps between subsidiary flows and parent treasury
FX options (call/put, European style) for contingent or uncertain trade flows; for re-invoicing entities, banks require proof of an identified commercial cross-currency risk

FX forward with a 'client preference' borrowing for hedging executed through the same counterparty with aggregator only if authorized by the CSSF-based conduct; alternatives like futures are not centrally cleared and not commonly used for trade intermediary

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, annexes and, if applicable, management report and auditor's report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 8 months of the financial year-end; for calendar-year accounts by 31 August
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court summons and criminal fine up to EUR 25,000; formal RCS notice followed by administrative strike-off; joint and several liability of managers for resulting damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; extensions may be granted by the ACD upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine up to EUR 25,000; monthly default interest of 0.6% on unpaid tax; enforcement against corporate assets and, in serious cases, director criminal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return and annual recapitulative statement for intra-Community supplies (as applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual VAT return due by 30 April of the following calendar year; monthly/quarterly periodic returns due by the 12th day of the following period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing administrative penalties up to EUR 25,000; default interest of 0.6% per month on VAT due; risk of forced assessment and denial of input VAT deduction in audit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner (RBE) declaration update and annual confirmation review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of any share transfer or change of beneficial ownership; no fixed annual anniversary filing, but annual reconciliation should be completed before the ordinary general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 10,000 and criminal penalties (including imprisonment up to 5 years) for false or omitted beneficial-owner information; publication of non-compliance for serious breaches.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL is subject to independent statutory audit if it exceeds two of three size criteria at the balance-sheet date: total assets above EUR 4.4m, net turnover above EUR 8.8m, or average workforce above 50 employees. Audit is also compulsory for listed companies, credit/financial institutions, insurance/reinsurance undertakings, collective investment vehicles and securitisation entities, regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Luxembourg Law of 19 December 2002 and the plan comptable normalisé; EU-adopted IFRS is permitted for consolidated financial statements and required for listed companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO renewal filing exists; however, the SARL must submit an updated RBE declaration within one month of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership. The registered agent should perform an annual reconciliation of the share register against the RBE declaration, document it in the corporate minutes, and retain a signed confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of members/shareholders (Registre des parts sociales)
Minutes of shareholders' meetings and managers' meetings
Original annual financial statements and supporting statutory accounting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 18,000 per year; not incurred where the small-company audit exemption applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (Luxembourg corporate income tax, impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, for fiscal years commencing on or after 1 January 2025; previously 17%. The effective aggregate statutory burden in Luxembourg City is approximately 22.80%, comprising 15% IRC, a 7% employment-fund surcharge on the IRC equal to 1.05%, and the communal trade tax, impôt commercial communal, at approximately 6.75%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption of qualifying dividend income and 80% exemption of qualifying capital gains on share disposals, subject to the 10% (or EUR 6,000,000 acquisition cost) holding threshold and the 12-month holding period. IP regime: 80% exemption of net qualifying intellectual property income. Allowance for Corporate Equity (notional interest deduction): deduction of 4.5% (FY2025), 4.0% (FY2026) and 3.5% (FY2027) on incremental new equity. Integral fiscal unity: resident group members may offset profits and losses. No withholding tax on outbound interest or royalties. Foreign tax credits available for foreign withholding taxes.
